get_current_sun_phase.description: Find out where the sun is at this moment at a place: whether it is daylight, twilight or night, whether the golden or blue hour is running, and which event is due next and in how many minutes, worked out by comparing the time now with the day's sun times. This is the check to branch a schedule on: switch something on at dusk, or send a reminder half an hour before sunset.

moonrise.description: When the moon first rises within the day. An ISO 8601 time with its UTC offset, or Unix seconds if you chose that time format. Empty on the day, about once a month, it does not rise.

moonset.description: When the moon last sets within the day. An ISO 8601 time with its UTC offset, or Unix seconds if you chose that time format. Empty on the day, about once a month, it does not set.

nautical_twilight_begin.description: Morning nautical twilight begins (the sun 12 degrees below the horizon): the horizon at sea becomes visible. An ISO 8601 time with its UTC offset, or Unix seconds if you chose that time format. Empty when it does not happen that day.

solar_noon.description: Solar noon: when the sun is highest in the sky. An ISO 8601 time with its UTC offset, or Unix seconds if you chose that time format. Empty when it does not happen that day.

solar_position.description: Where the sun is at sunrise, sunset and solar noon, from Sunrise Sunset.

solar_noon_altitude.description: How high the sun is at solar noon, in degrees above the horizon. Below zero when it stays under the horizon all day.

solar_noon_azimuth.description: Compass bearing of the sun at solar noon, in degrees clockwise from north.

sunset_azimuth.description: Compass bearing of the sunset, in degrees clockwise from north (270 is west). Empty when the sun does not set.

get_twilight_times.description: Get dawn, dusk and the three twilights for a place on one day, grouped into the morning and evening runs they belong to: first light, then nautical, then civil twilight, then sunrise, and back out the other way after sunset. Civil twilight is when it is light enough to be outdoors without a lamp; after astronomical twilight the sky is fully dark.

description: Look up sunrise and sunset times anywhere on Earth with the keyless Sunrise Sunset API. Get sun and moon events for a day or a whole year, the golden and blue hours for a shoot, dawn, dusk and the three twilights, the sun's compass bearing and height in the sky, how the day length is changing, and whether it is light out right now. Times come in the location's own timezone. No account or API key is required; showing a link to sunrise-sunset.org is.
